chapter: Last years of the band and reflections
title: Chambers books Dizzy Gillespie and the band must lay off
summary: On their return the Club Riviera owner gives their three weeks to Dizzy Gillespie, and Pillars and Jeter pay the musicians out of pocket.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: trip ended in New York City. And we had booked our band back in the Club Riviera. We had given Mr. Chambers the first three weeks of fall, in St. Louis. He took advantage of us, and let a booking agent book Dizzy Gillespie in for that three weeks, and that made us have to lay off for three weeks. And when all the band came back off of vacation, see, they all had a vacation in August, in July.

We met and came back -- they all came back to go to work in September. And Mr. Chambers had booked the other band, and we had given him his word that on our first day back in St. Louis, we'd be at his place. That meant that the guys had to lay off. That meant that Jean and I had to go in our pockets to kind of finance the guys, to help them along through those three weeks. Those are the headaches you have when you have a big band.
That's a funny thing, too. And everybody came back, I guess, about $15, $20,000 overseas, that did it.
